stories.title: At least 14 newborn babies killed in Pakistan hospital nursery fire
stories.summary: Prime minister orders investigation and promises ‘strictest action’ against those responsible for the blaze. At least 14 newborn babies have been killed in a fire that broke out in the nursery of a government-run hospital in Pakistan’s capital, Islamabad, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said, as he ordered an investigation. The fire broke out on Wednesday on the third floor of the Mother and Child Centre Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) hospital, according to media reports. Local broadcaster Geo TV, quoting hospital sources, put the death toll at 15. It said the blaze, which began shortly before 7am local time (02:00 GMT), has now been extinguished. Only one infant was rescued, it added. In a statement on X, Sharif offered his “deepest condolences to the bereaved families” and directed authorities to conduct “an immediate investigation”. He promised that those responsible would face the “strictest action”. Geo TV cited rescue sources as saying that the fire was likely caused by a short circuit in a malfunctioning air conditioning unit. Building fires are common in Pakistan, where safety regulations and building codes are routinely ignored or poorly enforced. In January, at least 65 people died when a massive fire swept through a crowded shopping complex in the southern port city of Karachi. Wednesday’s blaze is one of the deadliest hospital fires in Pakistan’s history.

stories.title: Pakistan ex-PM Imran Khan’s life is at risk in prison, sons say
stories.summary: Imran Khan’s sons claim his life is at risk due to harsh prison conditions and denied visits, urging international pressure on Pakistan for human rights violations. Khan is held in a small cell with limited light and no prisoner contact, prompting UN concerns that conditions may amount to torture. Pakistani authorities deny solitary confinement claims, citing security reasons and access to amenities; Khan’s health has sparked legal battles and public outcry. Former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan’s life is at risk due to the conditions of his prison confinement, his sons said during an emotional news conference on Aug 25, adding that efforts to visit their jailed father have hit a wall. “My father is the toughest person I know. But he is 73 years old, and his body is paying the price for how he is being treated,” Kasim Khan said during a press briefing via Zoom from London. “At this point its looking more likely than not that he won’t be able to survive this – his stay in prison.” Attention on Khan has intensified in recent weeks over concerns about his health. Earlier in August, the country’s top court ordered that he be transferred to a private hospital for medical treatment. The government challenged the order, and Khan was taken to a state-run hospital before being returned to Adiala Jail in Rawalpindi. A government spokesman said Khan was returned to prison after doctors found him in stable health. Elected as prime minister in August 2018 under a coalition led by his Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party, Khan was ousted less than four years later in a no-confidence vote amid a deep economic slump.
